title: Canonical scalar-extension point of a field-valued moduli object
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $p:\mathcal F\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ in the total-category convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Let $\Omega$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $x$ be an object of the strict fibre of $p$ over $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,g)$. In the iso-comma scalar extension $\mathcal F_\Omega$ of [def-sfb-moduli-scheme-base-change], form the object $(x,\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is the canonical isomorphism from the fibre equality $p(x)=(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,g)$ and $\mathrm{id}\circ g=g$. Define the scalar-extension point of $x$ to be the class of this field-valued object in the quotient of field objects by the equivalence relation generated by arrows, using [def-sfb-dm-stack-morphism-properties]. This is an explicit construction and assumes no algebraicity, adequacy or algebraic closedness.
